title: Harborlight Access Center
platform: Salesforce Health Cloud and Experience Cloud

sections.title: Data model and structural decisions
sections.html:
Three records carry the whole solution: the person, the referral, and the organization that sent it. The three choices below shape every section after this one, so they come first.

ObjectAPI nameUsed by
PersonAccount (person)Intake, Screening, Crisis follow-up{{D-01}}
ReferralReferral__cEvery capability{{D-02}}
Referring organizationAccount, record type PartnerIntake, Partner updates
Outreach attemptTaskAssignment, Crisis follow-up
Automation onWhenThe one ownerCapabilities that add to it
ReferralAfter saveOne flow, "Referral: after save"Intake, Screening, Assignment, Partner updates
ReferralBefore saveFormulas and validation rules onlyScreening, Assignment

Partner access. Partners sign in to a site and see only the referrals their own organization sent. {{D-03}}

sections.title: Referral intake
sections.html:
A referral reaches Harborlight three ways: the website, a partner, and fax. Each becomes one referral linked to the person and to the organization that sent it. SOW 2.1.

  1. Partner or member of the public submits the referral on the partner site, or on the public website form.
  2. System looks for the person by name and date of birth with a matching rule, and creates a Person Account only when there is none.
  3. System creates the referral with its source and the time it was received.
  4. System turns each email in the fax mailbox into a draft referral with the fax attached; the intake specialist reads it and fills in the fields. {{D-04}}
  5. Intake specialist checks it and moves it from Received to In review.
ElementSpec
RecordReferral (Referral__c)
Source valuesWebsite, Partner, Fax, Phone
DuplicatesMatching rule on first name, last name and date of birth; alert, not block

sections.title: Screening and eligibility
sections.html:
The intake specialist screens each referral against the four programs' eligibility rules and records which programs fit. SOW 2.2.

  1. Intake specialist answers the screening questions on the referral.
  2. System reads the eligibility rules from rule records an administrator can edit and proposes the programs that fit. {{D-05}}
  3. Intake specialist accepts the proposal or overrides it with a reason.

sections.title: Assignment
sections.html:
An accepted referral is assigned to a program and a site, and the site has two business days to make first contact. SOW 2.3.

  1. Intake specialist picks the program and the site.
  2. System sets the owner to the queue for that program and site. {{D-06}}
  3. Site coordinator takes it from the queue and logs each outreach attempt as a task.
  4. System shows the business days waiting with a formula; nothing is scheduled.

sections.title: Partner updates
sections.html:
A referring partner can find out what happened to a referral without calling the Access Center. SOW 2.4.

  1. Partner signs in to the site and opens the list of referrals their organization sent.
  2. System shows each one's status and nothing about care. {{D-07}}

sections.title: Crisis follow-up
sections.html:
When someone is discharged from crisis care, the crisis follow-up coordinator contacts them within one business day and books an appointment within seven. SOW 2.5.

  1. Coordinator finds the person and their earlier referral records.
  2. Coordinator starts a new referral linked to the closed one, so the history is one click away. {{D-08}}
  3. System counts the days to contact and to appointment from the new record's received date.

decisions.q: How a person seeking care is stored
decisions.ask: Do we turn on Person Accounts for the people Harborlight serves, or keep them as Contacts under an account?
decisions.why: Every capability reads or writes this record. It is the hardest choice to change later.
decisions.today: New org with Health Cloud. Person Accounts are not turned on yet.
decisions.reqs: R-02: one record per person across every referral they ever have.

opts.name: Person Accounts
opts.sum: One record is both the person and their account.
opts.gain: Health Cloud and the partner site are both built around it
opts.cost: Once turned on in an org it cannot be turned off
opts.risk: Any later work with organizations sits beside person accounts

opts.name: Contacts under an account
opts.sum: Each person is a Contact; a household account holds them.
opts.cost: Health Cloud care features need extra setup to work with plain contacts
opts.risk: The same person can end up under two accounts

decisions.lean_why: Health Cloud is in the SOW and its features assume it.
decisions.change_if: Harborlight plans to sell to or manage organizations in this org

decisions.q: What a referral is in Salesforce
decisions.ask: Is a referral its own object, a Lead that converts when accepted, or a Case?
decisions.why: Intake, screening, assignment, partner updates and the County report are all built on this record.
decisions.said: "The same person can come to us three times in a year, from three different places." Priya Nair, D1 00:22:10
decisions.reqs: R-05: every referral keeps its own source, dates and outcome.

opts.name: Its own object
opts.sum: A custom Referral record, many per person.
opts.gain: Each referral keeps its own dates and outcome, and the person keeps their history
opts.cost: No built-in web form; intake needs a flow

opts.name: A Lead that converts
opts.sum: A Lead until accepted, then converted to the person.
opts.cost: A person referred twice is two leads; declined referrals never reach the person record
opts.risk: History is split between leads and the person

opts.name: A Case
opts.sum: A Case with a Referral record type.
opts.gain: Queues, email intake and time targets are standard
opts.cost: Case fields and statuses are named for support and most need relabeling
opts.risk: Staff see service terms that do not match intake

decisions.lean_why: It is the only option that keeps one person with many referrals, which is what Priya described.
decisions.change_if: Harborlight only ever needs the latest referral per person

decisions.q: How partners follow the referrals they send
decisions.ask: Do partner organizations get a login to a site, or a public form with status sent by email?
decisions.why: It sets the access model and decides whether the partner updates capability is a site or an email.
decisions.today: Experience Cloud licences are in the SOW. No site exists.
decisions.reqs: R-11: a referring partner can find out what happened to a referral without calling.

opts.name: A partner site with logins
opts.sum: Partners sign in, submit, and see their own referrals.
opts.gain: Submitting and checking status happen in one place
opts.cost: Partner users have to be created and looked after
opts.risk: Sharing has to be exact: a partner sees only what they sent

opts.name: A public form and status emails
opts.sum: No logins. Status goes out by email when it changes.
opts.risk: Each email has to say very little

decisions.lean_why: The SOW already includes the licences and R-11 asks for look-up, not notification.
decisions.change_if: Harborlight cannot staff partner user administration

decisions.ask: Does the fax mailbox create a draft referral with the fax attached, or do staff keep keying faxes in by hand?
decisions.why: One step of the intake flow and the fax mailbox setup.
decisions.said: "I am not retyping a fax into two places." Linda Pham, D1 00:41:07
decisions.today: Faxes arrive as PDFs in a shared mailbox.
decisions.reqs: R-07: fax referrals are logged the day they arrive.

opts.name: The mailbox creates a draft
opts.sum: Each fax email becomes a draft referral with the PDF attached.
opts.gain: Nothing is lost in the mailbox; the received time is exact
opts.cost: Staff still read the fax and fill in the fields
opts.risk: Junk faxes create drafts that need closing
builds: email service on the fax mailbox

opts.name: Staff key it in
opts.sum: Staff open the mailbox and create the referral themselves.
opts.cost: Received time depends on when someone opens the mailbox

decisions.lean_why: R-07 needs the arrival time, and only the mailbox knows it.
decisions.change_if: IT cannot forward the fax mailbox to Salesforce

decisions.why: Four program directors own these rules and they change; an edit is a record change, not a flow change.
decisions.pick: Rule records an administrator can edit, read by one flow
decisions.alt: writing each rule into the flow

decisions.q: How an assigned referral reaches the right people
decisions.ask: Does the referral go to a queue for its program and site, or is it routed to an available coordinator?
decisions.why: The assignment step and how site coordinators find their work.
decisions.today: Sites work from a shared spreadsheet filtered by site.
decisions.reqs: R-14: a site coordinator sees new referrals for their site and program the same day.

opts.name: Queues by program and site
opts.sum: The referral flow sets the owner to a queue.
opts.gain: Simple to see and to change
opts.cost: Someone has to pick work up from the queue
opts.risk: A quiet site can leave work waiting
builds: a branch in the referral flow

opts.name: Routing to a person
opts.sum: Omni-Channel hands each referral to an available coordinator.
opts.cost: Coordinators must set themselves available; more to administer

decisions.lean_why: It meets R-14 with the least to build and maintain.
decisions.change_if: Volumes grow past what a site can pick up by hand

decisions.q: What a partner sees on the site
decisions.why: It answers R-11 and says nothing about care.
decisions.pick: Status only: Received, In review, Assigned, Closed

decisions.q: Crisis follow-up after a referral is closed
decisions.ask: When someone comes back through crisis after their referral was closed, do we reopen that referral or start a new one linked to it?
decisions.why: The crisis follow-up flow and the seven-day appointment measure on the County report.
decisions.said: "If they come back through crisis, it's a new episode for us, but I need to see the history." Javier Morales, D3 00:18:54
decisions.reqs: R-08: contact within one business day of discharge, appointment within seven days.

opts.name: Reopen the closed referral
opts.sum: One record carries the whole history.
opts.gain: Everything for the person in one place
opts.cost: Closed dates move, so time-to-close reports must allow for reopening
opts.risk: The seven-day measure needs a separate reopen date
opts.undo: Hard once records reopen in production

opts.name: New referral, linked to the closed one
opts.sum: Each episode gets its own record.
opts.gain: Clean dates and reports; matches how Javier describes it
opts.cost: Two records per person; history is one click away
builds: a lookup from the new referral to the earlier one
a related list on the page

decisions.lean_why: It matches the client's own words and keeps every date clean.
decisions.change_if: Harborlight reports episodes per person, not per referral

decisions.q: What a partner may be told once a referral is assigned
decisions.why: 42 CFR Part 2 limits what a referrer can be told. The status wording waits on her answer.
decisions.ref: Q-21, with the SC to ask Kim Tanaka

decisions.chosen: The standard Account, with a Partner record type
decisions.why_chosen: The standard object does the job.
Nothing to schedule or maintain, and it is always current.

decisions.chosen: Permission sets; no profile is edited
decisions.why_chosen: As narrow as the two staff roles in the SOW need.
Both are reported on, and neither has a process or layout of its own.
